title: Finite coefficient-root extension with an algebraically independent rooted tuple
statement: Let k→K be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] in one universe, let s be a finite algebraically independent subset over k [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], let p be prime with char(k)=p, and let P be any polynomial over E=k(s). There are fields l,L in that universe and commuting scalar towers k→l→L and k→K→L, with l/k and L/K finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and a finite algebraically independent subset t of L over l, such that E embeds in E₁=l(t), the embeddings E→K→L and E→E₁→L agree, every coefficient of P mapped to E₁ is a p-th power in E₁, and K together with E₁ generates L. No finiteness of K/E, finite generation of K/k, separability hypothesis, or degree inequality is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 04KM, coefficient-root construction in the induction step

proof.text: For an element x of E=k(s), induct on its membership in the intermediate-field adjoin to find a finite subset Cx of k such that any ring homomorphism f:E→F to a field of characteristic p sends x to a p-th power whenever it sends Cx and the generators s to p-th powers. For a generator use the variable-root hypothesis; for a constant c take {c}. For sums and products take the union of the two finite constant sets and sum or multiply the roots. For inverses use the inverse of a root. The identities (a+b)^p=a^p+b^p, (ab)^p=a^pb^p and (a⁻¹)^p=(a^p)⁻¹ verify every case. This is finiteConstants_for_element, proved locally without a hole.

Induction on a finite set of elements takes the union of their finite constant sets. Apply this to P.coeffs to obtain one finite C that suffices for every nonzero coefficient of P. This is finiteConstants_for_finset, proved locally without a hole.

Apply the finite rooted extension theorem to this C and s. It supplies finite purely inseparable l/k and L/K, an independent t, the algebra E→E₁=l(t), its scalar tower, roots of C in l, roots of s in E₁ and the compositum equality. Its proof constructs actual subfields of an algebraic closure; no data is taken from an unproved existence statement.

The maps k→E→E₁ and k→l→E₁ agree after embedding E₁ into L by the two scalar towers. Injectivity of E₁→L makes them equal. Map each constant root from l into E₁. The proved finite-constant criterion now gives a p-th root for every nonzero coefficient. A zero coefficient has root zero, since p>0. Assemble these conclusions with the extension and compositum data.

theorem exists_coefficientRoot_extension
    (k K : Type w) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (s : Finset K)
    (hs : AlgebraicIndependent k ((↑) : s → K))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (P : (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))[X]) :
    ∃ (l : Type w) (hl : Field l) (akl : Algebra k l)
      (L : Type w) (hL : Field L) (aKL : Algebra K L) (alL : Algebra l L)
      (akL : Algebra k L) (htl : IsScalarTower k l L) (htK : IsScalarTower k K L),
      Module.Finite k l ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k l ∧
      Module.Finite K L ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K L ∧
      ∃ t : Finset L, AlgebraicIndependent l ((↑) : t → L) ∧
        ∃ (a : Algebra (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))),
          IsScalarTower (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L)) L ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ b : IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L),
            algebraMap (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
              (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L)) (P.coeff n) = b ^ p) ∧
          IntermediateField.adjoin (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))
            (Set.range (algebraMap K L)) = ⊤
